sources.note: screen13 (Android Settings > App info, com.android.settings) was excluded by the tester as out of app: its 11 marked elements appear under screens with found_by 'none' and no verdicts, are not counted in elements_evaluated, and are listed with the tester's other detection false positives. Severity 'Low' is assigned where only personas hold the issue, every holder softened after testing, and the tester's own initial suspicion was overturned to Clear Purpose by its test. On an element with no issue, confidence is null unless the tester's Clear Purpose verdict itself was provisional.

screen1-a1.appearance: two horizontal lines, the lower one shorter
screen1-a1.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen1-a1.classification_basis: Gopal: cue "Only the two little lines. Nothing written."; why "Two lines are not a word. I have seen a stack of three lines mean 'menu' on other things, but this one has two, and I cannot be certain it is the same thing."; solution "Put the word 'Menu' next to the lines." -> Missing Purpose | Kwame: cue "Only the two-line picture in the corner; I have learnt that shape from other apps."; why "There is no word on it. I can guess it is a menu, but I cannot be certain what is inside, and I could not say its name aloud to my speech software."; solution "Put the word 'Menu' or 'Chats' under or beside the lines." -> Missing Purpose. Rule: a cue of nothing / a request to add a word reads as Missing; a word or picture that was there but did not help, or a request to change wording, reads as Unclear. For a picture-only control, a request to add a word or a cue of only the picture reads as Missing (the persona's solution decides when the reasoning supports both).

tester.deciding_evidence: tapping it slid a navigation drawer in from the left, exactly what the menu convention promises; the missing label is not a barrier

personas.expectation: Opens a side menu with the app's sections and my past chats.
personas.cue: The stacked lines, which is the usual menu picture, in the usual top-left place.
personas.why: It is the standard menu glyph and it sits in the same corner on every main screen.

personas.expectation: I suppose a list of choices would open, some sort of menu. I would be guessing.
personas.cue: Only the two little lines. Nothing written.
personas.why: Two lines are not a word. I have seen a stack of three lines mean 'menu' on other things, but this one has two, and I cannot be certain it is the same thing.
personas.solution: Put the word 'Menu' next to the lines.

personas.solution: Put the word 'Menu' or 'Chats' under or beside the lines.

screen1-a2.description: pill in the header with a sparkle glyph and the words 'Get Plus'

tester.deciding_evidence: tapping opened a paywall ('ChatGPT Plus', 'Upgrade for $19.99', 'Renews monthly') - a paid monthly subscription the words 'Get Plus' never mentioned
tester.recommendation: say what it is and that it is paid, e.g. 'Upgrade to Plus (paid plan)'

personas.expectation: Opens a page to buy a paid plan.
personas.cue: The words 'Get Plus'. I know from outside the app that Plus is a paid tier, but the button does not say that.
personas.why: 'Get Plus' does not say what Plus is, that it costs money, or that it is a subscription. The sparkle adds nothing literal.
personas.solution: Say it literally, e.g. 'Upgrade to paid plan (Plus)'.

personas.expectation: I think it wants to sell me something extra called 'Plus'. I expect a page asking me to pay.
personas.cue: The words 'Get Plus' and the sparkling star, which looks like advertising.
personas.why: 'Plus' is a product name, not an ordinary word. 'Get' tells me I would be acquiring something, but not what it is or whether it costs money.
personas.solution: Say it plainly, for example 'Buy a paid subscription' or 'See paid plans'.

personas.expectation: It takes me to pay for an upgraded version of the app.
personas.cue: The words 'Get Plus' and the sparkle star.
personas.why: The words say it. I know 'Plus' means the paid version.

personas.expectation: Takes me to buying the paid version
personas.cue: The words 'Get Plus' and the sparkle
personas.why: It says it outright - it's an upsell

screen1-a2.recommendation: say what it is and that it is paid, e.g. 'Upgrade to Plus (paid plan)' — personas asked for: Amy: "Say it literally, e.g. 'Upgrade to paid plan (Plus)'."; Gopal: "Say it plainly, for example 'Buy a paid subscription' or 'See paid plans'."

personas.expectation: Either starts a new chat or refreshes something. I cannot decide which.

personas.expectation: I honestly do not know. It could refresh the chat, start a new chat, or show chat history.

personas.solution: Put a clear word on it, such as 'New chat', or replace it with a plain pencil-and-paper or plus sign plus that word.

personas.solution: A short word under it like 'New chat' or 'Temporary', or the usual pencil-and-paper new chat icon
